subject: SIG questionnaire — confirmation on ephemeral logs and training opt-out
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nexacloud.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@nexacloud.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: retention & training opt-out clarifications

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on our initial SIG. A few follow-up items came up in our security review that we need clarified for legal and procurement before we sign. Could you confirm the below (we marked priorities):

1) Prompt and request logs: do you persist raw prompt text or model responses beyond the live request TTL? If yes, what is the default retention, and can a customer-specific retention TTL be enforced contractually? (high)

2) Use of customer data for model tuning: do you ever use customer prompts, responses, or derived embeddings to further train or fine-tune models in the hosted environment? If so, is there a documented opt-out? Describe the workflow and controls. (high)

3) KV cache / ephemeral context: aside from request logs, are any in-memory caches or KV stores persisted to disk or backups where customer content may end up? Describe eviction and persistence settings. (medium)

4) Deletion / on-demand purge: if a customer requests deletion of historical request logs, what is the SLA and process? Include any limitations (e.g., backups, audit trails). (medium)

5) Encryption and key management: clarify encryption at rest/in transit and whether customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported for logs/storage. (low)

If you can provide a short, plain-English answer for each and attach any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 summary, architecture diagram, or a redlined clause we can use for contract), that would help our procurement and legal teams.

Appreciate it — we are looking to finalize procurement next week.

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of Security & Compliance
NexaCloud

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com

Team — forwarding NexaCloud's follow-up. They highlighted five concrete asks; cc'd Vivek for product/runtime answers and Laura for security/legal wording we can share.

Short notes from me:
- We should be explicit that prompt logs are kept for 30 days by default in hosted, configurable down to 0 days with Dedicated/Private and contract language.
- We currently do not use customer requests/prompts for model tuning by default; opt-in only and only on Dedicated/private with explicit contract + data pipeline. Need confirmation from Infra on caches/eviction and from Security on BYOK.

Can you two draft a concise response and any supporting artifacts we can send (SOC2 summary + diagram)? Prefer to keep it under one page per question.

Thanks — Steph
Steph Nguyen
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up: retention & training opt-out clarifications

Steph / Vivek — Draft answers below that are customer-friendly and legally safe. I'm attaching a short SOC 2 summary and an updated architecture diagram to illustrate storage boundaries. Please review and let me know any product nuances to adjust.

1) Prompt and request logs:
- Plain-English: We do not retain prompt text or model outputs beyond the configured retention window. For hosted customers the default retention is 30 days; customers may contractually request a shorter retention or immediate purge. We support contract language to set retention to 0 days (ephemeral) for enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Note: For Hosted customers, metadata (request timestamps, model/route used) may be retained longer for billing and observability; we can redact or minimize metadata on request.

2) Use of customer data for model tuning:
- Plain-English: Customer prompts and responses are NOT used to train or fine-tune models by default. Model tuning using customer data is strictly opt-in and requires an explicit contract amendment, documented data pipeline, and customer approval. For Hosted customers we offer a managed "consent-based tuning" program that includes data isolation and a retention policy.

3) KV cache / ephemeral context:
- Plain-English: Runtime KV caches are in-memory for low-latency serving and are not persisted to durable storage by default. When we employ checkpointing for long-running sessions (rare), data is written to encrypted ephemeral volumes with automatic eviction. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can opt for in-memory-only configurations with no disk persistence.

4) Deletion / on-demand purge:
- Plain-English: Customers can request deletion of historical logs via console or support ticket. For Hosted customers, deletions are executed within 72 hours; for Dedicated/Private we target 24–48 hours depending on the environment and backups. Backups containing logs are rotated per backup retention policy; we will coordinate targeted restores and purges where feasible and document any residual audit entries.

5) Encryption and key management:
- Plain-English: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS1.3) and at rest using AES-256. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/BYOK) in Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we provide managed encryption keys with HSM-backed KMS.

Attachments to send:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level control map)
- redwood-data-architecture-diagram.png (storage boundary callouts)
- sample contractual clause for retention and opt-out (text below — legal to review)

Sample contract wording (suggested clause):
"Customer Data; Retention and Use
Redwood shall retain Customer Data (including prompts and model outputs) only for the retention period specified in the Order Form. By default, retention for Hosted customers is thirty (30) days. Customer may request a shorter retention period, including immediate deletion (0 days), subject to infrastructure availability. Customer Data shall not be used to train, improve, or fine-tune any model unless Customer provides explicit, written consent via a separate agreement amendment. Redwood shall promptly delete Customer Data from primary and secondary stores in accordance with the agreed retention schedule; residual backup copies will be deleted according to Redwood's backup retention policy or earlier upon request where technically feasible."

Vivek — if you can confirm the 30-day default and the 72-hour deletion SLA for Hosted, I will package and send to Alex with attachments.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Per Laura and Vivek below, please find concise answers to each item and the artifacts attached. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through with procurement/legal.

1) Prompt and request logs:
- Answer: We do not retain raw prompts or model outputs beyond the configured retention window. Hosted default: 30 days. Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): can be set to 0 days (ephemeral) contractually. Metadata for billing/observability may be retained; we can limit/minimize on request.

2) Use of customer data for model tuning:
- Answer: We DO NOT use customer prompts or outputs for model training by default. Any tuning that uses customer data is opt-in only and requires a signed amendment. Our managed tuning workflow includes a separate ingestion pipeline, tracking, and customer approval gates.

3) KV cache / ephemeral context:
- Answer: Runtime KV cache is in-memory and not persisted to durable storage under normal operation. Checkpointing (rare) writes to encrypted ephemeral volumes with automatic eviction; Dedicated/Private can be configured to be in-memory-only.

4) Deletion / on-demand purge:
- Answer: Hosted: deletions executed within 72 hours from request. Dedicated/Private: 24–48 hours targeted. We will coordinate targeted backup purges where feasible and document any residual audit entries.

5) Encryption and key management:
- Answer: TLS 1.2+/TLS1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest. BYOK (customer-managed keys) supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers get HSM-backed managed keys.

Attachments (attached to this email):
- NexaCloud_SIG_answers_v1.pdf (one-page Q/A)
- redwood-data-architecture-diagram.png (storage boundaries)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 high-level)

Next steps: if these answers are acceptable, Laura's suggested clause can be added to the MSA or an amendment. If NexaCloud requires a formal redline, please share and our legal team will prioritize.

Best,
Steph Nguyen
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
